prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2024 – Summary (≤500 words)

Overall aim: “Secure future” built on economic stability, lower taxes, controlled migration, stronger defence, better public services and community pride.

Economy and tax
- Keep public finances within fiscal rules (debt falling; borrowing <3% of GDP in year 5).
- Cut employee National Insurance to 6% by April 2027; abolish main rate of self‑employed NI by end of Parliament.
- Triple Lock Plus: both State Pension and pensioner tax-free allowance rise by the highest of inflation, earnings or 2.5%.
- No rises in the main rates of income tax or VAT; clamp down on avoidance/evasion to raise £6bn a year.
- Support SMEs: lighter reporting, improved access to finance, prompt payment enforcement, business rates relief, retain SME investment reliefs; no rise in Corporation Tax; extend full expensing to leasing when affordable.
- Invest in infrastructure (Network North), nationwide gigabit and 5G; rail reform via Great British Railways; drivers’ measures (no road pricing, reverse London ULEZ expansion, referendums for new 20mph/Low Traffic schemes).

Work, welfare and families
- 30 free childcare hours from 9 months to school start by Sept 2025; wraparound care by 2026.
- Reform Child Benefit to a household test: taper from £120k to £160k combined income.
- Welfare reform: tighter work capability and PIP assessments, fit notes moved to specialists, tougher sanctions after 12 months, anti-fraud bill; target £12bn annual savings.

Young people and education
- Mandatory National Service at 18: 12‑month military/cyber placements (paid, competitive) or one weekend a month civic service.
- 100,000 more apprenticeships funded by curbing low‑value degrees.
- Advanced British Standard for 16–19, English and maths to 18; mobile phones banned in school day; parental access to curriculum.

NHS and social care
- Real-terms NHS funding rises; 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors; shift care closer to home (Pharmacy First, 50 new Community Diagnostic Centres, 250 GP surgery upgrades).
- £3.4bn tech plan (AI, NHS App as single front door); cut managers by 5,500.
- Dental Recovery Plan: 2.5m extra appointments; new dentists to serve in NHS or repay training.
- Women’s health strategy; implement Cass Review; protect single-sex wards and intimate care.

Law, order and borders
- 8,000 more neighbourhood police; hotspot policing; tougher sentencing (rapists to serve full terms, more whole-life tariffs); Martyn’s Law for venue security.
- New extremism measures; stricter protest controls.
- Immigration: legal annual cap (falling each year), monthly Rwanda flights to remove illegal arrivals, tighter asylum rules, more returns deals. Skilled Worker salary thresholds up; health checks/IHS changes; higher visa fees.

Energy, climate and housing
- Net zero 2050 with “pragmatic” approach: no new green levies; treble offshore wind; annual North Sea licensing; new gas plants; expand nuclear (approve two SMR fleets; progress Wylfa/Sizewell/Hinkley); launch CCS clusters.
- Cut bills via market reforms, standing charge review, energy-efficiency vouchers; no fracking; onshore wind with local consent; prioritise rooftop/brownfield solar.
- Build 1.6m homes: fast-track brownfield, higher inner‑London density, protect Green Belt; permanent FTB Stamp Duty threshold at £425k; new Help to Buy; renters’ reform (end Section 21 after court changes); complete leasehold reform; CGT relief for landlords selling to tenants.

Rural, farming, environment and culture
- Increase UK farming budget by £1bn over Parliament; legal food security target; faster farm planning; renew £100m UK Seafood Fund; back inshore fleet.
- Plan for Water: tougher enforcement, river restoration; new National Park; more access to nature; tougher fly-tipping penalties; deposit return scheme.
- Invest in grassroots sport; independent football regulator; support creative industries and BBC impartiality review.

Defence and foreign policy
- Defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030; boost munitions, innovation and procurement; sustained support for Ukraine; strengthen alliances (NATO, AUKUS, CPTPP); uphold Windsor Framework; strengthen the Union with direct UK funding for devolved nations.
